questionText:
Consider the following ANSI C program.

Which one of the following options is correct?
options: The program will not compile successfully.
The program will compile successfully and output 10 when executed.
The program will compile successfully and output 8 when executed.
The program will compile successfully and output 13 when executed.
explanation:
Step 1: Code Trace & Variables
Initial values: $count = 0$, $i = 0$.
The loop runs for $j = -3$ to $3$.

Step 2: Execution Trace
• $j = -3, -2, -1$: The expression $(j \ge 0)$ evaluates to false. Due to short-circuit evaluation of the logical AND operator (&&), the second sub-expression $(i++)$ is not evaluated. Thus, $i$ remains $0$ and $count$ remains $0$.
• $j = 0$: The expression $(j \ge 0)$ evaluates to true ($0 \ge 0$). The second expression $(i++)$ is now evaluated. The post-increment operator returns the current value $i = 0$ (which evaluates as false in boolean context) and then increments $i$ to $1$. Since $true \&\& false$ is false, the body of the if statement is skipped. ($i = 1$, $count = 0$).
• $j = 1$: $(j \ge 0)$ is true. $(i++)$ returns $1$ (true) and increments $i$ to $2$. Since $true \&\& true$ is true, $count = count + j = 0 + 1 = 1$. ($i = 2$, $count = 1$).
• $j = 2$: $(j \ge 0)$ is true. $(i++)$ returns $2$ (true) and increments $i$ to $3$. $count = count + j = 1 + 2 = 3$. ($i = 3$, $count = 3$).
• $j = 3$: $(j \ge 0)$ is true. $(i++)$ returns $3$ (true) and increments $i$ to $4$. $count = count + j = 3 + 3 = 6$. ($i = 4$, $count = 6$).

Step 3: Final Output Calculation
After exiting the loop, the statement count = count + i; executes:
$count = 6 + 4 = 10$.

The program compiles successfully and prints 10.

Therefore, option (B) is the correct answer.
